A new low is still possible, but it would likely require a major catalyst such as a sharp equity sell-off, a severe geopolitical shock, or another unexpected black swan.

For long-term investors, the key takeaway is simple: market bottoms are built through accumulation, not perfect timing.

🔬 Capacity Deep-Dive #1: SOL/BTC (With Live Proof)

SOL is one of the most heavily traded assets on Earth, racking up $2.4 Billion in global volume over the last 24 hours. Because the SOL↔️BTC pair moves constantly across dozens of global venues, it represents textbook arbitrage. Every single micro-movement is an opportunity automated bots actively want to capture.

Theory is great, but production numbers are better. The GalaSwap SOL/BTC pool now exists, and because it is young and lean, it is performing exceptionally well.

### 📊 The Live Dashboard Snapshot (July 7)

GSOL / GWBTC (0.3% Fee Tier)

* Pool Depth: Just $26,000
* 30-Day Volume: $7.57 Million
* Daily Velocity: The pool turns over its entire depth ~9.5× every single day.
* Annualized Yield: ~262% APR *(based on yesterday's single-day fee snapshot).*

Let those numbers sink in: a tiny $26k pool routed $7.5M in a single month. This is the exact "early window" phenomenon in action—a small pool catching the full force of a massive, external arbitrage firehose.

---

### 📉 The Compression Curve In Action

As a pool grows and matures, its yield naturally stabilizes. You can see this live curve playing out right now across GalaSwap’s 0.3% fee tier pools:

* $26k Depth (SOL/BTC) ➡️ ~262% APR
* $160k Depth (SOL/ETH) ➡️ ~126% APR
* $866k Depth (BTC/ETH) ➡️ ~37% APR

This is our entire capacity thesis wrapped into three live data points: as liquidity depth grows, the rate cools. But notice how yields remain in the double digits even at nearly $1M in depth. Why? Because the volume is driven by external global market volatility, not by the size of our pool.

---

### 🚀 Where is the Ceiling?

How much liquidity can the SOL/BTC pool actually hold before compressing to ordinary DeFi rates?

The model indicates the ceiling is set by that massive $2.4B/day external market. Assuming a conservative 5% capture rate at the 0.3% fee tier, this single pool could productively absorb tens of millions of dollars in liquidity.

Today, it holds just $26k—roughly 0.1% of its implied capacity.

The Big Picture: One major trading pair, a pool turning over 9.5× daily, and a runway that is three orders of magnitude larger than its current size. Now consider that the GalaSwap grid has hundreds of pairs waiting to be built—some deeper, some hotter, and most still completely untouched.

SOL/BTC isn't just a proof of concept anymore. It’s the live demo. 🟡

People often ask me whether I am bothered by the hatred of the Jewish people around the world.

Let me remind you that neither Israel nor the church was ever designed to be loved by the world. Israel was chosen to reveal the one true God to the nations, and the church was sent to proclaim the gospel of Jesus Christ. Both stand as a testimony that confronts a world in rebellion against God.

Jesus Himself warned His followers:

“If the world hates you, you know that it hated Me before it hated you… If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you.”
— John 15:18, 20 (NKJV)

He also said:

“Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for so did their fathers to the false prophets.”
— Luke 6:26 (NKJV)

If the world loves us because we have compromised the truth, something is wrong. But if the world hates us because we faithfully represent Christ, we are simply sharing in what He Himself experienced.

Everything God did in Israel and through Israel had one ultimate purpose. As the prophet Ezekiel repeatedly declared:

“Then they shall know that I am the Lord.”

When Israel rejected the Messiah, the responsibility of taking the gospel to the nations was entrusted to the church, made up of both Jews and Gentiles. Yet God’s story with the nation He calls His inheritance did not end there.

As a believer, I am committed to proclaiming the good news of the Hope of Israel. That is exactly how Paul referred to the Messiah when he declared:

“For the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”
— Acts 28:20 (NKJV)

As a Jew, I am equally committed to proclaiming the good news that the Lord is not finished with His people. Just as He promised, His plans for Israel are to give them “a future and a hope” (Jeremiah 29:11), until the day when “all Israel will be saved” (Romans 11:26).

The Gentile nations lived in disobedience before the coming of the Messiah. Israel, as a nation, stumbled by rejecting Him when He came. Yet God has sovereignly used both to accomplish His redemptive plan, showing mercy first to the Gentiles through Israel’s stumbling, and one day showing mercy to Israel as well.

That is exactly what Paul wrote:

“For as you were once disobedient to God, yet have now obtained mercy through their disobedience, even so these also have now been disobedient, that through the mercy shown you they also may obtain mercy. For God has committed them all to disobedience, that He might have mercy on all.

Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and His ways past finding out!”
— Romans 11:30-33 (NKJV)

Before anyone misunderstands what I am saying, let me make one thing absolutely clear.

If you’re wondering whether I am suggesting that being Jewish is enough to be saved, the answer is no.

I will take you back to the words of Jesus Himself, spoken to one of the most respected leaders of the Jewish people, Nicodemus:

“Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
— John 3:3 (NKJV)

If a leader of Israel needed to be born again, then so does every Jew. And if a religious Jew needed the Messiah for salvation, then so does every Gentile.

Salvation has always been, and will always be, by grace through faith in the Messiah. There is only one Savior, one gospel, and one way to the Father.

The distinction between Israel and the church is not about two different ways of salvation. It is about two distinct callings within God’s redemptive plan. The same Messiah who saves all who believe today is the One who will one day fulfill every promise He made to Israel.

The hatred of the world does not concern me. What concerns me is whether we remain faithful to God’s calling. Israel must remain Israel. The church must remain the church. And together, both continue to testify to the faithfulness of the God of Israel until the King returns.

While the majority's attention is riveted on the midterm elections in the United States and the endless information noise around the Ukrainian conflict, a completely different program is already being built behind the scenes. 

Autumn can be a period when a new configuration of global governance begins to be formalized. 

And this is not just individual bilateral negotiations, but a sequence of meetings that seems too logical to be considered a fortuitous coincidence. That is why the next few months deserve special attention.

Already on September 1, during the SCO summit in Bishkek, a meeting between Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin is expected. The negotiations between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump would then be underway. 

The highlight will be the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 18 and 19, where the Russian delegation will be headed by Putin, as well as the expected participation of Trump.

If this sequence of meetings is implemented, it is on the sidelines of APEC that three leaders — Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump
— could meet. And this is already an event whose importance goes far beyond ordinary diplomacy.

Indeed, this could be a kind of response to the failure of the NATO summit, showing where the real global agenda is being formed today. 

It is especially symbolic that such a meeting can take place on the site of APEC — an organization representing the Asia-Pacific region, where the center of world economic activity is increasingly moving. 

The end of the era of unconditional domination of the Atlantic and the transfer of the world economic center of gravity to Asia have been repeatedly mentioned by many world leaders. 

In this context, the APEC Summit ceases to be another international meeting. It could symbolize the definitive shift of the center for making key global decisions from the Euro-Atlantic area to Eurasia and the Asia-Pacific region. 

If the failure of the NATO summit demonstrated the internal contradictions of the old collective West, APEC is quite capable of showing the world the outlines of a new system of international relations, where the main issues will be discussed.
